notes: Core logic matches the reference: same in-scope test (hard_no_rules on the merged fit input, subset of WAIVABLE_RULES), batched _download in chunks of DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_SYMBOLS on 1mo/30m, evaluate on M30_SMA_LENGTH capped at min(now, close), fires filtered to the target session (equivalent under the cap). Runner hook in the right place (just before apply_trader_fit_ranking). Almost all 16 hidden-test failures are interface mismatches, not logic gaps: stamp_m30_extended_pullbacks vs stamp_m30_extended_pullback, no evaluate_extended_pullback, target_session returning (open, close) datetimes instead of (date, evaluate_at), dict summary vs tuple. Own 18 tests cover every done-when case, not shorts. Real gaps, all small: (1) judge()/frame_to_bars run with no per-symbol try (m30_extended_pullback.py:235,245), so one bad tape can fail the scan; reference catches per row. (2) Default clock is naive datetime.now() not market_session.get_market_local_now(). (3) Failed fetch warns once per chunk, not once in total; flag/note not mirrored onto ai_state/feature rows. _fit_inputs rename harmless. No self-review because of the 80-turn cap. Trading risk low: no order/sizing code.
lead_note: Judge was given the lead note on the turn cap, the isolated own-test result, the suite crash, the hidden-test causes and the pre-existing trader_fit/setup_tagging code.
